title: auth-api-401-429-debug-scratchpad-lena-2026-03-22
content:
Objective: quick scratchpad for the 401/429 behaviour observed across hosted API endpoints. Use this to collect commands, logs, hypotheses and next steps before filing a cleaner incident report.

Symptoms observed:
- Intermittent 401 responses starting ~2026-03-21 22:18 UTC for client X (prod key). Happens ~1-2% of requests, mostly to /v1/chat/completions.
- 429 spikes later in the day (2026-03-22) after deploy, broader client base. 429s include Retry-After header sometimes, sometimes not.
- Other endpoints (embeddings, rerank) less affected.
- No obvious billing failure in account dashboard.

Commands / repro attempts I ran:
1) Capture response headers with curl (raw):
   curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \n     -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \n     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n     -d '{"model":"openchat-7b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'

   Observed sample 401 response (curl -i):
   HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
   Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 22:43:10 GMT
   Content-Type: application/json
   Content-Length: 123
   Connection: keep-alive

   {"error":{"message":"Invalid API key","type":"auth_error","param":null,"code":null}}

2) Same call with -v to see TLS and connection: no TLS errors, handshake fine.

3) Tried passing key as query param (not recommended) to test backend path:
   curl -i "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions?key=$API_KEY" \n     -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{...}'
   -> 401 as well. Indicates auth check happens in front of route.

4) Python requests quick-check: (used requests.session to reuse conn)
   import requests
   s = requests.Session()
   r = s.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions', headers={'Authorization':f'Bearer {API_KEY}'}, json={...})
   print(r.status_code, r.headers.get('x-request-id'))
   -> 401, x-request-id: req-6f4a2b

5) Checked header casing/whitespace: trimmed token, ensured no stray quotes. Same result.

6) Rate-limit repro: I wrote a small loop to send ~200 requests/min with valid API key: observed 429s after ~120 requests within a 60s window. Sample 429 payload: {"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded","type":"rate_limit_error"}}
   Response headers when 429 provided (varies):
     Retry-After: 10
     X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
     X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
     X-RateLimit-Reset: 17110826

   However some 429s showed none of the limit headers (frontend drop).

Logs / correlated IDs I pulled:
- req-6f4a2b (401) 2026-03-22T22:43:10Z client_ip=35.187.12.4 client_id=acct-prod-42 route=/v1/chat/completions auth_check=failure reason=key_not_found
- req-7a9c1d (429) 2026-03-22T23:02:05Z client_ip=35.187.12.4 client_id=acct-prod-42 route=/v1/chat/completions quota_window=60s used=121 limit=120

Notes from logs: some 401s show reason=key_revoked and some say key_not_found. Timestamps overlap with a key rotation event recorded in GH ops-log (see linked artifact).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Key rotation / partial rollout: a subset of our edge servers got an updated key mapping where some keys are missing or outdated — explains intermittent 401 with key_not_found / key_revoked.
2) Incorrect or stale cache in auth-service: auth-service caches tenant->key mapping and may have stale entries after a database migration. Explains sudden 401 spike correlated with deploy.
3) Rate limit config mismatch: chat endpoint has a stricter per-minute limit (120/min) vs embeddings (higher). A sudden traffic shift (cron job on client using chat) led to 429s. Some edge proxies drop headers when they hit global rate limit bucket, hence missing X-RateLimit-* headers.
4) Billing/blocked account for some clients: but dashboards show account active — low probability.
5) Downstream auth-db replication lag causing transient key_not_found.

Immediate mitigations tried / suggested:
- Recreate repro with curl using suspect key and capture x-request-id; forwarded to SRE with timestamp + id.
- Scoped test: rotated a non-prod key and saw consistent 401 until rotation fully propagated -> suggests rotation propagation issue.
- Added exponential backoff retries for 429s in client to reduce load.
- Temporary quota bump for acct-prod-42 requested via internal console (pending).

Client-side recommendations to ship quickly:
- Implement client-side retries for 429 with exponential backoff and jitter. Use Retry-After header when present.
- Avoid bursty cron-style requests to chat endpoint; batch or stagger.

Next steps / action items:
- [ ] Add full list of affected request-ids and timestamps to JIRA INF-2345 (Samir doing).
- [ ] Check auth-service cache invalidation logs around 2026-03-21 22:00-23:00 UTC (Oliver).
- [ ] Confirm whether key rotation job had partial failures (release-engineering). Link: GH issue in linked_artifacts.
- [ ] Add better observability: surface X-RateLimit-* headers in frontend responses even when global bucket rejects (Product/Platform).
- [ ] Short-term: issue org-level quota increase for acct-prod-42 if customer impact continues.

Open questions / things to verify:
- Why do some 429s not return rate-limit headers? proxy vs global limiter? Need SRE to confirm.
- Why do 401 reasons vary between key_not_found and key_revoked? Are we mixing rotated+reclaimed keys?
- Any traffic pattern change on client side? confirm with customer.

Scratch notes / quick commands saved: 
- capture headers with curl: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions | sed -n '1,20p'
- get request-id and call internal logs: ./infra-tools/logs --id req-6f4a2b --since 1h

Tail thought: this feels like two related but separate issues — auth mapping/rotation causing 401, and unrelated but concurrent rate-limit saturation causing 429. Both surfaced because traffic shifted to chat endpoint after a deploy.

I'll keep adding request-ids and timestamps here. Once we have a clean list we'll attach to INF-2345 and loop in SRE + release-engineering.

-- Lena
